text:
Maria: Heads up — CI flagged a perf regression on PR 13876. Microbench warmup p99 up ~18% vs golden. Kernel autoselect flipped to generic path for some seq lengths. attaching CI link: <https://ci.redwood/13876/bench>
Ajay: link looks noisy but the threshold diff is real: 
```
batcher_timer.p99: baseline=23.4ms new=27.6ms (+18%)
kv_cache.hitrate: baseline=0.72 new=0.41 (-43%)
```
ci-bot: perf-regression-bot: +18% p99 detected for //runtime:micro_warmup; threshold-exceeded; report id perf-2026-173333.
Lee: I pulled the flamegraphs from the failing run. there's a big spike inside `kernel_selector::evaluate` and then a long hot loop in `batcher::wait_and_dispatch`.
Lee: flamegraph excerpt:
```
kernel_selector::evaluate (42.1%)
  heuristics::cost_model (28.3%)
    quant_selector::score (12.7%)
batcher::wait_and_dispatch (18.9%)
  kv_cache::lookup (10.2%)
```
Sam: KV hitrate drop matches what I see in the CI logs — lots of cold misses during warmup, seems like earlier cache affinity tweak evicted popular prefixes.
Maria: The suspicious commit range is the kernel-autoselect refactor (commit d4e5f6a7..a1b2c3d4) merged in PR 13870 about 2 days before this PR. That PR adjusted the cost weights for preferring fused kernels.
Ajay: bisect plan: git bisect between v2026-03-01 (good) and HEAD (bad) with the CI bench runner. Command: `git bisect start HEAD v2026-03-01 && git bisect run ./scripts/ci_perf_bench.sh --target micro_warmup`
Jia: Will try to repro locally on a P4 instance. Local reproducer: `./dev/bench/runtime_warmup --seq-len=128 --iters=1000 --profile flamegraph` — flamegraph produced will match CI if it's deterministic.
perf-bot: Note: microbenchers can be noisy; run 3x and compare medians. Also check `--no-jit` flag for parity with CI container.
Ajay: If bisect shows the autoselect refactor, can we gate the new heuristics behind an env var? e.g., `RW_ENABLE_AUTOSELECT=false` to force old selector for now.
Maria: I'll open a rollback PR that flips the env var default and add a rollout gate. If that stabilizes CI we'll push a fast revert. Creating PR now.
Sam: Also need to verify Dedicated/Dedicated-staging profiles — warmup behaviors differ under reserved pools. I'll run the reproducer there after the rollback.
Maria: quick debug note — observed kernel selection decisions in the failing trace: `seq_len 64 -> chosen generic; seq_len 128 -> chosen fused` for same workload where baseline always chose fused. That smells like a cost-normalization bug introduced in d4e5f6a7.
Ajay: +1 to revert if bisect isolates it. If revert is slow, we can ship an immediate temp fix: set cost weight `pref_fused = 1000` in runtime config to bias fused.
ci-bot: rollout-blocked: requires perf sign-off or revert PR to proceed with current merge queue.
Maria: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/13902 (temporary-autoselect-disable). Triggering CI now. I'll follow up with CI links in this thread. cc @Ajay @Lee
Ajay: Thanks — I'll start the bisect in parallel and post results. If anyone sees a quick repro locally, paste the flamegraph and the `git rev-parse --short HEAD`.
Maria: CI started on PR 13902: run id ci-1733330140. If that passes and microbench medians look back to baseline, we'll merge and unblock the queue.
Sam: :thumbsup: keep an eye on KV metrics after the env var change, might need to tune cache affinity separately.
Maria: CI passed on PR 13902 (ci-1733330140). micro_warmup medians back to baseline in two runs. I'll land the PR and announce rollback in releases. Follow-up ticket to properly fix cost-normalization is filed: ENG-3371.
ci-bot: perf-note: regression mitigated by temporary rollback; please follow up with root-cause bisect and permanent fix.
Maria: Thanks everyone — will close the loop in ENG-3371 once we have a deterministic bisect and a proper patch.
